You're shocked when you finally see it. At first it's just a shimmering in the distance, a golden wink brief enough to have been imagined, like sunlight glinting off a shard of glass in the tumbling surf. 

Peering through your scopes, the shimmer takes form: a golden penumbra limning a perfect circle growing as you draw near. The shape comes in flashes now, here and gone in a fraction of a second, each sight somehow freighted with the experience of lifetimes, yours, yes, but also somehow others, past and future generations living and dying in an instant.

name: 79AU_DreamOne
title: Dream of the Golden Beacon
desc:
You've never seen a persimmon. In fact, you're only remotely aware of what a persimmon is. But in your dream, the one that comes to you every time you close your eyes, you're certain that's what you're looking at. 

The orange fruit is dangling from a crooked branch on an otherwise barren bush growing atop a hill overlooking miles of scrubland. High morning sunlight warms your body and flashes gold as beams pass through the dew glistening on the flesh of the berry.

You reach for it, and suddenly it shrinks from your view. The entire bush in fact races away, zooms out for miles, hundreds of them, thousands, the fruit now so distant as to be off-world, a far-flung orbiting body, a golden pinprick in the now night sky shining bright as Polaris and radiating just the same significance.

It is a way point. A guiding light. A signal fire lit in an ancient brazier from a torch held by someone you've never met but you're certain you know. 

You stare at the distant gold-winking light in the otherwise black sky and awaken with a cold certainty that you know exactly where it lies: 79au. The object calling to you in your dreams orbits Sol at 79au. And you know you have to find it.

name: PLOT_79au_StartTrigger_DreamOne
title: Trigger for the 79au Plot Start Beat
desc: Beginning of the 79au plot.

name: 79AU_NightOse
title: Choose President Ose
desc:
"Him," you say, and point towards President Ose in the corner. "Or ... that. I choose that."

A cold silence invades the room. Emerald sinks down into her seat, shoulders slumped, arms limp. Fire slams an open palm onto the table so hard the glassware rattles. 

"Now now. Don't be cross," Ose says, and stands up from the table. "It's just a game, after all."

The VIPs at the wet bar gather themselves and exchange brief goodbyes as they file out of the room. Emerald, Fire and Sanguine move to join them. 

"See you later?" you try. 

Fire looks back at you. "I sincerely hope not," she says, and then leaves the room after the others. 

"Don't worry about her," Ose says, and gives you a wink. "She's very competitive." 

You look around the room, empty now besides you, Joakim and Ose, who has his hand outstretched to admire his perfect manicure. 

"The pair has been chosen," Joakim says. "Who will begin?"

"Me," says Ose, and then claps his hands twice.

You feel a nearly imperceptible rumbling beneath your feet, here for just a moment and then gone. You look to Ose, who shows a fanged grin.    

"Show me out, would you?" Ose says.

You travel with Ose to the elevator, and sit there for what feels like an eternity as the lift reaches your floor. Your companion is far from the curious and seductive conversationalist he was before. In fact, he seems utterly indifferent to your existence.

The elevator dings and Ose steps inside.

"What's next?" you ask him.

"That, you'll find, is entirely up to you." Ose says. The doors close before him, and you're alone again. More alone than you've felt in a very long time. 

You take the elevator down to the lobby and find Joakim, who points you in the direction of your ship. He's very graciously topped off your reactor with enough fuel to make the trip home, a courtesy he informs you is granted to all visitors of the hotel. 
  
Following Joakim's directions, you wheel yourself down a long corridor that seems to grow darker and longer as you travel. The trip is so long that your mind begins to wander after the architecture of this strange place, and just as it does you find yourself in the bridge of your ship, with no recollection of ever traveling through an airlock. 

Finding no real reason to stay, you plug in coordinates towards home, and your ship begins the long return journey.
